module: Applies thrust to the vehicle: jbeam thrusters ('thrusters' section, driven by an electrics value or in 'auto' mode which produces a thrust proportional to the relative speed between two nodes), force impulses between two nodes, and imposed accelerations/velocities on a cluster of nodes. A modder or a tool (scenarios, script) uses it to push or throw a vehicle for a given duration. The module is only active in the physics loop when there is something to apply.
usage:
-- push the vehicle forward (inferred: rear base -> front) for 0.5 s
thrusters.applyImpulseBody(5000, 0.5)
-- impose an acceleration of 20 m/s² upward for 0.2 s
thrusters.applyAccel(vec3(0, 0, 20), 0.2)
notes: jbeam keys of a thruster (v.data.thrusters): id1 (source node), id2 (destination node), control (name of an electrics value, or 'auto'), factor (1 by default), thrustLimit (max thrust in N, infinite by default). The applied force is min(electrics[control]*factor, thrustLimit) on the node pair (id2, id1), computed in updateGFX and applied at each physics step.

'auto' mode: vel = -speed of node id2 relative to id1; if vel > 0.3 m/s, thrust = vel² * factor, capped by thrustLimit; if other thrusters are active, the force measured between the nodes is added (max(0, force)). Note: factor and thrustLimit have no default for auto ones (only the activeThrusters path initializes them): without factor or thrustLimit defined, the arithmetic or the comparison may fail.
A control that does not exist in electrics causes an error log only once (invalidThrusterControlWarned); it is recommended to use vehicle bindings or an electrics channel.

applyImpulse/applyImpulseBody/applyAccel activate update() (physics); when nothing is active any more, M.update goes back to nop and updateCorePhysicsStepEnabled() is called again to disable the physics step.

Bug/inconsistency: applyImpulse and applyImpulseBody replace dt with lastDt (`dt or lastDt`) only when the impulse already exists; for a new impulse they insert the raw dt; if dt is nil, thruster[4] is nil and the computation `ttl - physicsDt` in update() raises an error. Always pass dt.
Units: forces in N, accelerations in m/s², speeds in m/s, durations in s; angularAccel is an angular acceleration (rad/s², vec3).
lastDt and physicsDt, updateCorePhysicsStepEnabled are game global variables (not defined in this file).

update.desc: nop, or this module's physics function when at least one thruster, impulse or cluster is active. Called at each physics step. ⚠ nop is a game global.

updateGFX.desc: nop, or the function that recomputes the electrics-driven thrusts each graphics frame if the vehicle has jbeam thrusters.

init.desc: Loads the vehicle's jbeam thrusters (split into auto and controlled), resets the impulses and chooses update/updateGFX. If the vehicle has no thrusters, sets both to nop.

reset.desc: Identical to init (M.reset = init): reinitializes the thrusters.

isPhysicsStepUsed.desc: Indicates whether the module is currently called at each physics step (M.update == update).

returns.desc: true if there are thrusts in progress.

applyImpulse.desc: Applies a constant force between two nodes for dt seconds; if the impulse already exists for this node pair, updates its force and duration.

n1.desc: Node (cid) to which the force is applied first.

dt.desc: Duration in seconds (must be provided: see bug in notes).

applyImpulseBody.desc: Like applyImpulse but between the vehicle's ref node and back node (refNodes[0].ref and .back), i.e. along the longitudinal axis of the chassis.

applyAccel.desc: Imposes a linear (and optionally angular) acceleration on the cluster of nodes containing nodeId for dt seconds (obj:applyClusterLinearAngularAccel). Only one acceleration per nodeId at a time: a new call replaces the old one.

accel.desc: Linear acceleration in m/s² (modified in place at the end of the duration).

nodeId.desc: Node of the cluster (ref node by default, or 0).

angularAccel.desc: Angular acceleration in rad/s² (zero by default).

applyVelocity.desc: Makes the cluster reach a given speed over a duration dt, by applying the acceleration (velocity - current speed excluding wheels) / dt. Does nothing if dt is 0.

nodeId.desc: Node of the cluster (ref node by default).

getAccelDt.desc: Returns the remaining duration of an acceleration applied by applyAccel/applyVelocity on this node.

returns.desc: Remaining duration in seconds (0 if there is none).
